elements.name: km-editor
elements.description:
---


### **Events:**
 - **change** - The document changed by the user (typing, toolbar, paste, …), a plugin, or `setValue()` (not `{ isSilent: true }`). Assigning `value` / `contentFormat` is silent, like a native `input.value`, and so is a form reset (like a native `form.reset()`). `detail`: `{ value, contentFormat }` — the content serialized in the active `contentFormat`. Twin: `onChange(detail)`.
- **ready** - The editor was built and is live for the first time (once per element lifetime; core `BlissElement`). Fires right after the first build — during upgrade for a normal element, or when the `defer` gate is released (`el.release()` / removing `defer`). The host then has the `ready` attribute and matches `:state(ready)`; `el.whenReady()` resolves. `detail`: `controller` / `element`. Twin: `onReady(detail)`.
- **view-mode-change** - The view mode was switched by anything but the app's own assignment: a view-mode toolbar item (`source: 'user'`), `setViewMode()` on the element or `controller` (`'api'`, unless `{ isSilent: true }`), or a plugin / pipeline stage through its `setViewMode` port (`'plugin'`). Assigning `viewMode` (attribute `view-mode`) is silent. `detail`: `{ viewMode, oldViewMode, source }`. Twin: `onViewModeChange(detail)`.
- **lock-change** - A gating pipeline (e.g. the cloud-image `image:browser:pick`) locked the editor for its run, or released it. `detail`: `{ isLocked }`. Twin: `onLockChange(detail)`.
- **value-format-error** - A `getValueFormatCallback` threw while formatting the submitted value. The hidden input then carries an empty string and the host is invalid (`customError`, message = label `valueFormatError`), so the form refuses to submit (`<form novalidate>` submits an empty string); the next successful format clears it. `detail`: `{ error, value }` (`value` = the unformatted document in `contentFormat`). Twin: `onValueFormatError(detail)`.
- **action** - A toolbar / selection-toolbar / context-menu item was activated. `detail`: `action` (the command name, or `custom`), `id`, `item`, `source` (`toolbar` | `selection-toolbar` | `context-menu`), `sourceEvent`, `triggerElement`, `dataset`, `state` (the ProseMirror state). Fires after the item’s `onClick` and the command (a notification after the fact; `state` is the snapshot from activation); `beforeActionCallback` → `false` cancels. Keyboard shortcuts do not fire it. Twin: `onAction(detail)`.
- **input-rejected** - Fired when a written value is refused (core, SPEC §6): an invalid attribute or property value, or an unknown `setAttributes()` key. The element warns and keeps its previous value. Detail `{ configKey, attribute?, value, reason?, kept, source }`. Twin callback `onInputRejected`.

### **Methods:**
 

- **formResetCallback(): _void_** - The surrounding `<form>` was reset: restore the initial content (`defaultValue`,
attribute `value`), like a native control — silently: a native `form.reset()`
fires no `input` / `change`, so neither does this (the hidden input is synced).




- **setValue(value: _string_, format: _EditorFormat_, options: _{ isSilent?: boolean }_): _void_** - Replace the document with `value`, parsed in `format` (defaults to the active
`contentFormat`) — the controller's write path. Fires `change` unless
`options.isSilent`; assigning `el.value` is the silent form (like a native
`input.value`). Either way the hidden form input is synced.
- **setViewMode(mode: _EditorViewMode_, options: _{ isSilent?: boolean }_): _void_** - Switch the view mode (`edit` | `split` | `preview` | `inline`). Fires
`view-mode-change` (`source: 'api'`) unless `options.isSilent`; a no-op (no event)
when `mode` is already active, and an invalid mode warns and keeps the current one.
Assigning `el.viewMode` is the silent form.

- **whenReady(): _Promise<void>_** - Resolves once the first build is live (also settles when the element is destroyed first). Never rejects.
- **release(): _void_** - Build an element held by `defer` (SPEC §6.3), with everything assigned meanwhile.
- **setAttributes(values: _Record<string, unknown>_): _InputRejection[]_** - Apply many inputs (by configKey or attribute name) as ONE rebuild / update. Returns the values it refused (each also fires `input-rejected`).
- **batch(fn: _() => void_): _void_** - Run `fn` and coalesce every input change it makes into one rebuild / update.
- **flush(): _void_** - Apply pending input writes synchronously, now (SPEC §12.7).
- **whenSettled(): _Promise<void>_** - Resolves once every staged input change has been applied (SPEC §12.7).
- **destroy(): _void_** - Final teardown (SPEC §6.5): the element is inert afterwards; idempotent.
- **enableLogging(level: _LogLevelDesc_): _void_** - Set this element's own log level (default `debug`): it logs that level and above, whatever its component type or the page is set to.
- **disableLogging(): _void_** - Silence this element (its own level = `silent`).
- **resetLogging(): _void_** - Clear this element's own log level: it follows its component type / the page again.
- **checkValidity(): _boolean_** - Form validity check (SPEC §6.6).
- **reportValidity(): _boolean_** - Form validity check that reports to the user (SPEC §6.6).

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: Initial / default content, interpreted per `contentFormat` (like a native input’s `value` attribute ↔ `defaultValue`). Changing it replaces the document. The live content is the `value` PROPERTY.

attributes.name: content-format
attributes.description: The format of the one document — the lens for content I/O (the `value` attribute and property, the `change` event): 'markdown' (default), 'html', or 'json'. Switching it re-reports the SAME document in the new format — it never rebuilds the document, and (like any assignment) fires no `change`.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Form field name. When set, a light-DOM `<input type="hidden" name="…">` child of the host carries the live content (serialized in `contentFormat`) and submits with the surrounding `<form>`; it is disabled (not submitted) while the editor is disabled, including by a `<fieldset disabled>`. A form reset restores `defaultValue` (attribute `value`) silently — no `change`, like a native `form.reset()`.

attributes.name: view-mode
attributes.description: Presentation: 'edit' (default), 'split' (editor + live output), 'preview' (read-only render), or 'inline' (overlay chrome on a live-page element). `preview` forces read-only. Full layouts arrive in Phase 3; for now the view mode is stored and reflected. Assigning it (property or attribute) is silent — no `view-mode-change`; `setViewMode()` and the view-mode toolbar items fire it.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description: Read-only: the content can’t change (no typing, toolbar hidden), but it stays focusable, selectable and copyable. `view-mode="preview"` also forces this on. Reflects to `readonly`.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disabled: no interaction at all — not editable, not focusable or selectable (the surface is `inert`), toolbar hidden. An ancestor `<fieldset disabled>` disables it too (core). Reflects to `disabled`, like a native control.

attributes.name: toolbar
attributes.description: Static toolbar edge: 'top' (default), 'bottom', 'start', or 'end' places the command toolbar flush against that side of the editor; 'none' hides it. The selection toolbar and context menu are always available while editing (independent of this).

attributes.name: statusbar
attributes.description: Status bar edge: 'none' (default), 'top', 'bottom', or 'both'. A dedicated strip of live indicators (word/char count, plus any plugin status items), hugging the editor body — separate from the toolbar zones and shown in read-only too. With 'both', items split across the two strips by their `bar` ('top'/'bottom', default 'bottom').

attributes.name: theme
attributes.description: Forced colour scheme: 'dark' swaps the token set (`:host([theme='dark'])`); 'light' (or unset) is the default look. Reflected to the host attribute.

attributes.name: anchor
attributes.description: For `view-mode="inline"` only: a CSS selector for the live-page element the floating editor card anchors to (tracked via the core positioning primitive). Absent → the inline card renders in normal flow.

attributes.name: labels
attributes.description: Every UI string (rulebook D-NC-24), a PARTIAL object over built-in English, `{name}` placeholders; an empty string = deliberately empty. `placeholder` (default empty = off) is shown while the document is empty. Command items: the camel-cased command id is the item text (`insertLink`, `bold`, `imageBrowserPick`), `<key>Tooltip` its tooltip; toolbar groups `<groupId>Group` (`formatGroup`, …); status `words` / `chars` (`{count}`); prompts `linkUrlPrompt`, `imageUrlPrompt`, `imageAltPrompt`, `codeLanguagePrompt` / `codeLanguageChangePrompt` (`{languages}`); cloud image `cloudImage`, `cloudImageTooltip`, `insertCloudImage`, `cloudImagePickerTitle`, `cloudImagePickerMessage`. Property (object) or JSON attribute (`labels='{"bold":"Tučně"}'`). Applies live (no rebuild).

attributes.name: custom-styles
attributes.description: CSS injected into the editor's shadow root (a `<style class="we-custom-styles">` after the page-wide `window.components['km-editor'].customStyles` layer, so it overrides it). An `@import`ed font is also linked once in the document `<head>` (core). Raw CSS — never put untrusted input here.

attributes.name: defer
attributes.description: Hold the first build (core, SPEC §6.3): while set when the element first connects, nothing is built and every input, callback and listener assigned meanwhile accumulates; `release()` (or removing the attribute) then builds once. Latched after the first build.

attributes.name: theme-source
attributes.description: Where this element reads its theme from instead of the page (core, SPEC §12.10): a CSS selector (nearest matching ancestor, else the first match), `'closest'` (the nearest ancestor carrying a theme signal), or (property only) an `Element`. Unset = the page.

attributes.name: motion
attributes.description: Motion level (core, SPEC §12.16): `auto` (default — inherit: the nearest `data-motion` ancestor (a section), else the page level `window.components.motion` / `<html data-motion>`; closest wins), `none` (no transitions, instant scrolling), `snappy` (short) or `smooth` (longer). Sets the shared `--base-duration-*` / `--base-scroll-behavior` tokens on the element through `data-motion`; the OS reduced-motion setting always wins.

attributes.name: responsive
attributes.description: Instance responsive rules (core, SPEC §6.7): partial configs on two axes — `device` (keyed by device class `mobile` / `tablet` / `desktop`; a mouse device is `desktop` at any width) and `breakpoint` (keyed by the window-width bucket); the breakpoint entry applies first, the device entry over it (device wins). An object or a JSON attribute, e.g. `{"device":{"tablet":{"presentation":"modal"}},"breakpoint":{"mobile":{…}}}`. Beats page rules (`window.components.responsive*`) and values set on the element; never reflects. An entry of `null` ignores the page rules while it matches.

properties.name: value
properties.description:
The live content, serialized in the active `contentFormat` (`''` before the first
build). Assigning replaces the document, parsed in `contentFormat` — like
`setValue(value, undefined, { isSilent: true })`: silent (no `change`, like a
native `input.value`); the hidden form input is synced. The `value` ATTRIBUTE is the initial content
(defaultValue) and is never written.

properties.name: plugins
properties.description:
The editor plugin set. Assign to customise — compose with `defaultPlugins()`
to keep the built-ins, and order the array to control conflict precedence
(later plugins override earlier by id). Reassigning rebuilds the engine on the
new set, preserving the live content. Reading returns the active set.

```js
import { defaultPlugins } from '@keenmate/web-editor';
el.plugins = [...defaultPlugins(), myPlugin];
```

properties.name: defaultValue
properties.description: Initial / default content, interpreted per `contentFormat` (like a native input’s `value` attribute ↔ `defaultValue`). Changing it replaces the document. The live content is the `value` PROPERTY.

properties.name: contentFormat
properties.description: The format of the one document — the lens for content I/O (the `value` attribute and property, the `change` event): 'markdown' (default), 'html', or 'json'. Switching it re-reports the SAME document in the new format — it never rebuilds the document, and (like any assignment) fires no `change`.

A form reset restores `defaultValue` (attribute `value`) silently — no `change`, like a native `form.reset()`.

properties.name: getValueFormatCallback
properties.description: Property only. `(ctx) => string` — formats the value written into the hidden form input (`name`), e.g. to sanitize HTML. `ctx`: `{ value, contentFormat }` (the document in the active `contentFormat`) + `controller` / `element`. Affects ONLY the submitted form value: `el.value` and the `change` detail stay the document in `contentFormat`. Called on every sync of the form input (each change). A throw is logged (error), the hidden input gets an empty string, the host turns invalid (label `valueFormatError`) and `value-format-error` fires; the next successful format clears it.

properties.name: beforeActionCallback
properties.description: Property only. `(detail) => false | void` (may be async) — runs first on every toolbar / selection-toolbar / context-menu activation, with the `action` event detail. Return `false` to cancel: no `onClick`, no `action` event, no command. Keyboard shortcuts do not pass through it.

properties.name: renderLoadingCallback
properties.description: Property only. Draws the pending loader (shown while a deferred pipeline's work — e.g. a cloud-image upload — outlives its loader threshold; not while a dialog waits for the user) instead of the default spinner: `({ component, context, containerElement, element, label }) => void | cleanup`, `context` = `'pipeline'`. Fill `containerElement` (it already has `role="status"` + `aria-label` = label `loading`); a returned function runs when the loader is removed. Beats the page-wide `window.components.renderLoadingCallback` (core SPEC §12.14). Read each time the loader shows.

properties.name: interactionHost
properties.description: Property only. The modal bridge interactive pipeline stages call: `{ request(ctx) }`, `ctx` = the request (`kind`, `title`, `message`, `payload`) + `signal` + `controller` / `element`. Default: a `window.confirm`-backed host. Survives engine rebuilds (e.g. a `plugins` reassignment).

properties.description: CSS injected into the editor's shadow root (a `<style class="we-custom-styles">` after the page-wide `window.components['km-editor'].customStyles` layer, so it overrides it). An `@import`ed font is also linked once in the document `<head>` (core). Raw CSS — never put untrusted input here.

properties.name: getCustomStylesCallback
properties.description: Property only. `(ctx) => string | null` — computes the instance CSS (wins over `customStyles`); `ctx` = `controller` / `element`. Called on every build and whenever `customStyles` / `getCustomStylesCallback` change.

properties.name: shouldDefer
properties.description: Hold the first build (core, SPEC §6.3): while set when the element first connects, nothing is built and every input, callback and listener assigned meanwhile accumulates; `release()` (or removing the attribute) then builds once. Latched after the first build.

properties.name: responsiveCallback
properties.description: Instance computed responsive rule (core, SPEC §6.7): `(ctx) => partial config | null | undefined`, ctx `{ env, deviceClass, breakpoint, element, component, config }` (`config` = base). Runs after `responsive` (wins key by key); re-runs on environment flips, throttled viewport-width changes, rule and config changes. `null` ignores every page rule.

properties.name: isReady
properties.description: The first build is live (core, SPEC §6.3) — the `ready` event has fired.

properties.name: isDestroyed
properties.description: `destroy()` ran.

properties.name: form
properties.description: The owning form (form-associated components).

properties.name: validity
properties.description: Form validity (SPEC §6.6).

properties.name: validationMessage
properties.description: Form validation message (SPEC §6.6).

properties.name: willValidate
properties.description: Whether the element takes part in form validation.
